canonical_statement: This prespecified secondary analysis evaluated whether the cardiovascular, kidney, physiologic, and selected safety effects of dapagliflozin varied according to baseline use of ACE inhibitors/angiotensin-receptor blockers, beta-blockers, diuretics, or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.
The analysis included 17,160 participants with type 2 diabetes and either established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors.

population.label: DECLARE-TIMI 58 randomized population

canonical_statement: Eligible participants had type 2 diabetes, established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors, and creatinine clearance of at least 60 mL/min.

population.label: DECLARE-TIMI 58 eligibility
inclusion_criteria: Established ASCVD or multiple cardiovascular risk factors

canonical_statement: Participants assigned to active treatment received dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily in addition to usual care.
Participants in the control arm received matching placebo in addition to usual care.
DECLARE-TIMI 58 was a randomized, double-blind, multinational, placebo-controlled trial; this report was a prespecified secondary subgroup analysis.
Efficacy analyses used the intention-to-treat principle; selected safety analyses used participants who received at least one dose, with prespecified on-treatment risk windows.

Treatment effects across baseline cardiovascular-medication subgroups were estimated with Cox proportional hazards models and treatment-by-subgroup interaction tests; no multiplicity adjustment was applied.
The analysis evaluated Cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that dapagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure and kidney disease progression with a consistent safety profile irrespective of baseline cardiovascular medication use.
The subgroup analyses were not powered to establish event reductions within individual medication subgroups or treatment-by-subgroup interactions.
Background medication doses were not recorded, preventing dose-dependent interaction analyses and detailed assessment of dose changes.
Because this was not a heart failure trial, the mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist subgroup was small and no participants used sacubitril/valsartan at baseline, limiting those analyses.
Baseline characteristics differed according to cardiovascular-medication use; randomization applied to dapagliflozin versus placebo, not to the background medication exposures.
The analysis could not establish a causal relationship between dapagliflozin-mediated changes in cardiovascular medications and clinical outcomes.
No adjustment for multiple comparisons was made, so nominal subgroup interaction findings require caution.
The DECLARE-TIMI 58 trial was supported by AstraZeneca.
The article reports extensive author financial relationships with industry; one author was an AstraZeneca employee and shareholder.
The article directs readers to Supplement 3 for the Data Sharing Statement; Supplement 3 was not present in the retrieved Drive folder.

The underlying DECLARE-TIMI 58 protocol specified a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3b study of approximately 17,150 participants at about 1,200 centers, with dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily versus placebo and planned median follow-up of approximately 4.5 years.

The protocol specified a two-step primary testing strategy: first demonstrate noninferiority for MACE with an upper hazard-ratio margin of 1.3, then test superiority for MACE and cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

The protocol renal composite included sustained >=40% eGFR decline to below 60 mL/min/1.73 m², end-stage renal disease, or renal or cardiovascular death; this differs from the kidney-specific composite used in the 2022 secondary analysis.
The protocol required participants to be at least 40 years old with type 2 diabetes and either established cardiovascular disease or prespecified cardiovascular risk factors.

canonical_statement: The protocol used a placebo run-in before randomization and scheduled repeated clinic and telephone follow-up through study closure.

Protocol safety surveillance included serious adverse events, discontinuation events, suspected cardiovascular events, neoplasms, hepatic events, major hypoglycemia, fractures, renal events, volume depletion, hypersensitivity, urinary tract infection, and genital infection.

The statistical analysis plan targeted approximately 17,150 randomized participants and 1,390 MACE events; it stated >99% power for the MACE noninferiority test, approximately 85% power for a true MACE HR of 0.85, and approximately 87% power for a CV death/HHF HR of 0.80 with about 770 events.
